name: Biren BR104 GPGPU (single-die inference accelerator)
architecture: Biren SPC (single die, half-size sibling of BR100)
memory_bandwidth_basis: None available. The BR104 is described as the 'half-size sibling of the BR100 for inference workloads' with 32 GB HBM2e at 300 W TDP, but no memory bandwidth figure is published in any source located. The BR100's 1.6 TB/s cannot be halved to derive the BR104's bandwidth because the memory subsystem may not be a simple halving.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: the BR104 is the inference-oriented sibling of the BR100, with half the memory (32 GB vs 64 GB) and roughly half the TDP (300 W vs 550 W). It is a single-die part, not a 2-die chiplet like the BR100. The BR104 shipped in place of the BR100 after TSMC halted all Biren manufacturing in October 2022 and Biren was added to the BIS Entity List in October 2023. The BR104 uses the BIRENSUPA software stack. No compute throughput figures are published for the BR104 in any source located — the BR100's 1024 TFLOPS BF16 / 2048 TOPS INT8 are 2020 launch-release figures for a different part and must not be carried over. The BR104 is significant because it represents Biren's pivot from a training-focused part (BR100) to an inference-focused part (BR104) under supply chain pressure. Vendor is 'asic-other' because 'biren' is not in the schema enum.
